skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Automate Twitter/X posting, media sharing, engagement, direct messages, follows, deletes, and lookups through the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.summary: Run guided Twitter/X automation workflows with the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.author: infsh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command hits are Markdown formatting, app identifiers, or code-fence boundaries rather than Ruby backtick execution. Several belt and npx examples are confirmed because they run external CLI actions with network, account, or installation side effects. Semantic review also found broad belt permissions and social-account automation that require explicit user approval.

remediation.suggestion: Replace Bash(belt *) with the narrowest supported command patterns, or require confirmation for every belt command before execution.
Add explicit approval, target account confirmation, rate-limit guidance, and X policy checks before posts, deletes, DMs, follows, likes, or retweets.
Mark npx skills add commands as optional manual steps and pin trusted sources or versions where possible.
Use local marketplace assets when possible and make external install documentation clearly user-initiated.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Social Account Automation
semantic_findings.description: The skill enables posting, liking, retweeting, deleting posts, sending DMs, and following users. These account-mutating actions can publish content, spam users, or alter an account if run without explicit consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The app table and command examples explicitly cover public posts, engagement, DMs, follows, and deletion. No approval, rate-limit, or abuse-prevention guard is present in the skill text.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad CLI Permission Scope
semantic_findings.description: The allowed-tools declaration grants Bash(belt *), and the skill also points users to browse all apps. This permits more belt subcommands than the documented Twitter/X workflow requires.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Line 4 directly uses a wildcard belt permission, while line 148 encourages app discovery. The permission scope is broader than the listed X app actions.

content.value_statement: Managing X posts and engagement by hand slows launch and community work. This skill provides guided belt CLI workflows for posting, media sharing, engagement, DMs, follows, and lookups.
actual_capabilities: Posts text updates to Twitter/X through the belt CLI.
Creates media posts when a media URL is provided.
Likes, retweets, deletes posts, sends DMs, and follows users.
Looks up user profiles and tweet details by identifier.
Shows workflows for generating image or video assets before posting.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and a configured Twitter/X integration.
Does not include built-in approval gates, rate limits, or policy checks.
Account actions depend on the connected X account permissions.
Media workflows require asset URLs from separate generation tools.

use_cases.title: Launch Communication
use_cases.description: Prepare and publish approved launch posts, media updates, and follow-up engagement from one CLI workflow.

use_cases.title: Developer Advocacy Updates
use_cases.description: Share release notes, demos, and community replies while keeping a clear approval step before public actions.

use_cases.title: Creator Content Operations
use_cases.description: Combine generated images or videos with short post copy and publish them through an authenticated X account.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Twitter automation skill to draft a short X post from this announcement. Ask for approval before running any command.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Media Post
prompt_templates.scenario: Posting with an existing media URL
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a post plan with concise text and this media URL. Show the proposed action, then wait for my approval.

prompt_templates.title: Review Engagement Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: For these tweet IDs, recommend which posts to like or retweet and explain why. Run only the actions I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Campaign Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a one-week X campaign using posts, profile checks, and media assets. Include approval checkpoints before each external action.

output_examples.input: Post our launch note about the new analytics dashboard.
output_examples.output: A concise post draft, an approval request, and a note that publishing will happen only after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Share this product screenshot URL with a short update.
output_examples.output: Post copy, a media attachment summary, and a confirmation checklist for the target account and audience.

output_examples.input: Review these tweet IDs for possible engagement.
output_examples.output: A recommended like or retweet plan with reasons, skipped items, and a request for approval before any action.

best_practices: Get explicit approval before posting, deleting, sending DMs, following, liking, or retweeting.
Confirm the target account, audience, and X policy requirements before running CLI actions.
Keep a record of approved commands, inputs, and published content for audit purposes.
anti_patterns: Do not automate likes, follows, retweets, or DMs at scale without user consent.
Do not publish confidential, unreleased, or third-party material without review.
Do not run broad belt commands when a specific reviewed action is needed.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Twitter/X posting, media posts, likes, retweets, deletes, DMs, follows, and lookups through inference.sh belt commands.

faq.question: Does it require a Twitter/X account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires an inference.sh setup with a connected X integration and account permissions.

faq.question: Can it post images or videos?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill shows media-post workflows that use a media URL from another tool or service.

faq.question: Can it schedule tweets?
faq.answer: It can be used inside scheduled workflows, but SKILL.md does not show a native scheduling command.

faq.question: Is unattended automation recommended?
faq.answer: No. Public posts, DMs, follows, likes, retweets, and deletes should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
